title: The Missing Pages

evidence.name: Torn Edge
evidence.text: A strip of paper cut from a bound book, with stitching holes. Waxed linen thread, hand-sewn. Someone cut the pages out with care.

evidence.name: Ferry Stub
evidence.text: A Douglas to Liverpool ticket stub, used as a bookmark in the Gaiety's pantomime script. The sort of thing everybody on the island has in a pocket.

evidence.name: Waxed Thread
evidence.text: A reel of waxed linen thread and a binder's bone folder on a plank under the Up Helly Aa galley. The same thread as the holes in the torn strip.

evidence.name: Collector's Card
evidence.text: A card from a Manx collector who buys old ledgers, pinned in the Jersey tunnels' visitors' book. He gets around. He is also a dealer in postcards, which is a different kind of crime.

evidence.name: Repair Receipt
evidence.text: A Guernsey museum receipt: the Channel Islands sheets were posted to a binder in Lerwick 'for re-sewing'. They went on purpose, with permission.

suspects.name: The Ferry Purser
suspects.wrong: Missing pages? I check tickets, not footnotes. Liverpool to Douglas is four hours and a bacon roll, not a heist.

suspects.name: The Ledger Collector
suspects.wrong: Me? I buy old ledgers, I do not borrow them. Besides, I would never take a ledger with only three pages in it. Where is the profit?

suspects.name: Halcrow the Binder
suspects.right: Ach. Caught. The Shetland and Mann sheets came to me in October for re-sewing, the Guernsey ones followed by post, and then it was the galley and the torches and the Jarl's cloak, and they have been under that bolt of canvas ever since. I never took them anywhere. I just stopped looking. I will finish the sewing by Candlemas.

steps.text: Take on Miss Quayle's case at the Gaiety, Douglas.
Search the prompt corner at the Gaiety.
Search the galley shed in Lerwick.
Question Halcrow the Binder in the galley shed.
Read the repair receipt in the Guernsey Occupation Museum.
Hear the Museum Volunteer in Guernsey.
Hear the Tunnel Historian at the Jersey War Tunnels.

accuse_hint: Miss Quayle is waiting at the Gaiety Theatre in Douglas.
closed: The pages are home, the Roll is whole, and the theatre ghost has been formally cleared.
